HISTORY & PHYSICAL (DETAILED)

Consult Summary:
27-year-old man with 3-day history of profuse watery diarrhea, mid-abdominal cramps, nausea/vomiting, and subjective fever consistent with acute infectious gastroenteritis; advised oral rehydration, symptomatic care, and 48-hour safety-net follow-up.

History:
• Presenting complaint: “Watery diarrhea” for 3 days.  
• Frequency: Approximately every hour while awake.  
• Stool characteristics: Watery; denies blood.  
• Abdominal pain: Crampy, mid-lower abdomen, intermittent, ~6/10, precedes each bowel motion.  
• Associated symptoms: Nausea; occasional vomiting (worse after milk); feels “very hot” (no temperature recorded); urine output reduced.  
• Onset/Timeline: Began Monday/Tuesday (3 days ago); ongoing without improvement.  
• Exposures: Brother with similar illness x 5 days. No recalled high-risk food intake.  
• Relieving/aggravating factors: Milk triggers vomiting; no specific relief noted.  
• Review of systems: No rectal bleeding, no constant severe abdominal pain, no known weight loss.

Past Medical History:
• Denies chronic medical conditions.  
• No previous bowel disease reported.

Medications:
• Paracetamol – dose/route/frequency not documented (used for fever/pain).  
Allergies:
• No known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives with mother and sister; brother lives separately.  
• Occupation: Government office worker in Central London.  
• Smoking: Social smoker (occasional cigarette, mainly Fridays).  
• Alcohol: Occasional beer during weekdays; heavier drinking 1–2 times/month; advised to avoid during illness.  
• Diet: Often buys food outside home; currently limited intake due to illness.

Family History:
• Father: Colon cancer (stage III).  
• Brother: Current similar diarrheal illness (improving).

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded (patient subjectively feels febrile).  
• General/Abdomen/Other systems: Not examined (tele-consult).  
• Overall impression: Appears systemically unwell per history; possible mild dehydration.

Investigations:
• None performed or ordered at this visit.

Assessment & Plan:

Overall Impression:
Most likely acute infectious gastroenteritis (likely viral; possible foodborne) causing high-volume watery diarrhea with risk of dehydration.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Gastroenteritis – Supported by abrupt onset, watery diarrhea, crampy pain, nausea, family member affected. No blood or chronic features oppose.  
2. Food poisoning – Possible common exposure with brother; absence of identified contaminant slightly opposes.

Issue 1: Acute watery diarrhea / suspected gastroenteritis  
Plan:  
• Oral rehydration: Advise OTC electrolyte solution (e.g., Dioralyte) per package directions.  
• Hydration goals: Encourage frequent small sips of clear fluids; monitor urine output.  
• Diet: Start with clear fluids → soft foods (soup, mashed foods) as tolerated; avoid dairy temporarily.  
• Symptom control: Continue Paracetamol as needed for fever/aches.  
• Activity: Rest; avoid alcohol and smoking until recovered.  
• Red flag advice: Seek urgent care if unable to keep fluids down, signs of dehydration (dizziness, very low urine), bloody stools, persistent fever, severe abdominal pain, or worsening symptoms.  
• Follow-up: Telephone review in 48 hours or sooner if deterioration.

Issue 2: Dehydration risk  
Plan:  
• Reinforce fluid/electrolyte replacement.  
• Consider in-person review, vitals, and basic labs (U&E, FBC) if no improvement or worsening at 48 h.

Issue 3: Family history of colon cancer  
Plan:  
• Documented; not contributory to acute illness.  
• Patient education: Discussed that current symptoms are most consistent with infection; no alarm features of malignancy.  
• Routine screening: Will revisit appropriate colorectal screening guidelines at future preventive visit.

General plan items:  
• Medical certificate/work note if required.  
• Encourage avoidance of food preparation for others until 48 h symptom-free to prevent spread.

Quality checks:
● Missing elements: No objective vitals or physical exam performed; allergy, medication list obtained but doses/frequencies incomplete.  
● No conflicts noted between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality acceptable; some conversational noise but clinically adequate.
